claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine whether you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To get started, could you please tell me **how many children** you're inquiring about, and **what are their names**?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one son named Alex.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

**First, how old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. And is Alex still in full-time education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, he actually left school recently, but he's just signed up with the careers service to figure out what he wants to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see, thank you for clarifying that. A couple of follow-up questions to help me understand Alex's situation better:

**Is Alex currently registered with the careers service as part of a formal government-recognised scheme, such as the Youth Support Service or similar programme that provides approved training or education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right. He registered with them recently after leaving school to get help figuring out his next steps.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Now I need to understand your personal circumstances as the claimant.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK?** (This relates to your right to reside in the UK.)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. Just to clarify further - **are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status under the UK immigration rules?** This is important for determining eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment.

**Are you currently living with Alex, and is he dependent on you for financial support?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One more important question:

**Since Alex left school, has he been in any paid work or apprenticeship, or is he currently only registered with the careers service while not working?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at the moment - just registered with the careers service.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have all the details I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the situation:
- Alex is 17 years old
- He recently left school but is registered with the careers service
- He is living with you and dependent on you
- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- He is not currently in paid work

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, children can qualify until age 19 if they're in approved education or training. Being registered with the careers service as part of a government-recognised scheme for support after leaving school typically qualifies as approved training under Child Benefit rules.

Since Alex meets the criteria (he's under 19, registered with an approved scheme, and you're a qualifying British citizen), you should be eligible to claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's a summary of why:
- Alex is 17 years old and therefore eligible under the Child Benefit age rules
- He is registered with the careers service, which is an approved training/support scheme
- You are a British citizen with the right to reside in the UK
- Alex is living with you as your dependent

You should be able to proceed with your Child Benefit claim. If you need to apply, you can do so through the official government channels. Is there anything else I can help clarify for you?
